Definition
[Algebraic and strong convergence] \group thurston.ch09.convergenceSource: thurston:page-0241Source: thurston:page-0242 For a countable group $\Gamma $ and representations $\rho _i:\Gamma \to G$, algebraic convergence means pointwise convergence $\rho _i(\gamma )\to \rho (\gamma )$ for every $\gamma $. Strong convergence means algebraic convergence together with geometric convergence of the image groups to $\rho (\Gamma )$.
